text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Representatives of the Turkish Ziraat Bank negotiated with National Bank of Macedonia governor Ljube Trpeski on the possiblity of opening a branch office in Macedonia. The idea is almost a year old and is within the frameworks of Macedonia's financial legal regulations.
- Macedonian parliament has appointed Branko Naumovski, former assistant justice minister, as the first ombudsman in the Republic of Macedonia.

- Investigation of financial scandal over collapsed TAT pyramid savings scheme in Bitola finally completed. The assets of the bankrupt savings society slightly over 53.47 million German marks, while liabilities are 111.984 million. Assets cover liabilities only 47.74 percent, leaving a "financial hole" in TAT of 58.5 million marks. Personal tax evasion of 8.9 million marks discovered. The mortgage value that TAT has demanded is 35 million marks.

- Macedonian government is seriously reviewing the World Bank proposal for reducing maternity leave from the current nine to three months. In its letter to the World Bank, the government said it is ready to make these steps to reduce general consumption, which is one of the conditions of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank for continuing financial support of Macedonia. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
